title: Start-up, data folder, settings file, audit writes and task queue robustness
owns: app/main/settings.ts, autostart.ts, logger.ts, app/main/agent/tasks.ts, app/main/policy/audit.ts, start-up/single-instance and crash handling in main.ts and windows.ts (small hunks)

findings.title: A failed audit write (disk full, quota, read-only or root-owned audit file) leaves the task queue half-updated: a task the user was told failed runs later, and finished tasks stay on screen as "Working…" forever
findings.area: main process robustness / low disk (agent TaskManager + AuditLog)
findings.scenario: The disk fills up (or the audit file/folder is unwritable, e.g. root-owned after a past sudo run). (a) The user asks for a task: TaskManager.start() queues it, then audit.write('asked') throws before pump()/publish() (tasks.ts:122-124). The conductor tool call fails, so the user is told it failed, but the task sits in the queue with no card. When space is freed and the user asks for something else, pump() starts the old task too and Ember acts in the user's apps on a request it said had failed. (b) A task is already running when writes start failing: finish() (tasks.ts:277) throws before publish()/onFinished()/the removal timer, so run() rejects before worker.dispose() and pump() (tasks.ts:258,267). The card shows "Working…" for ever, nothing is spoken or notified, and any queued task never starts. Only a restart recovers.
findings.evidence: Real app under xvfb, driven with Playwright and the offline mock model (scripts h/pw-audit-mid.mjs, h/pw-audit-phantom.mjs, h/pw-audit-full.mjs in the scratch folder). Healthy control: task done in 233 ms. (a) Audit file replaced by a directory before asking: bubble says 'Failed to execute start_task … Tool execution failed', task manager = ['Job A:queued'], 0 cards. After removing the obstacle and asking only for task B: manager = ['Job A:done','Job B:done']. (b) Audit made unwritable while 'Job number 1' and '2' run (3 queued): ember.log shows two 'unhandled rejection … EISDIR … audit-2026-10.jsonl'. For the next 14 s the overlay cards stay ['Job number 1:running','Job number 2:running'] while the manager says done/done and 'Job number 3:queued' never starts. No unit test covers an audit write that throws.
findings.fix: Never let an audit failure break bookkeeping. Make AuditLog.write catch and log.warn once (keep a bounded in-memory buffer if wanted), or at least wrap the two TaskManager writes in try/catch. In start(), pump()/publish() must not depend on the audit line. In run(), use try/finally so worker.dispose() and pump() always run, and finish() must publish before it audits. If the action path should stay fail-closed, keep that in worker.audit() only and cancel the task with a plain message.

findings.title: Ember exits silently (exit code 0, no window, no message) when its data folder can't be locked or written; it is treated as 'another Ember is already running'
findings.area: startup in odd environments / single instance
findings.platforms: all (reproduced on linux); any OS where userData is unwritable
findings.scenario: ~/.config/ember (or %LOCALAPPDATA%\ember) is not writable: owned by root after an earlier `sudo ember` that kept HOME, a read-only or immutable home, NFS root-squash, no free inodes. Chromium cannot create SingletonLock, so app.requestSingleInstanceLock() returns false and main.ts:128-131 logs 'instance.handover' and calls app.quit(). The log folder can't be created either (logger.ts:63 falls back to stderr), so a launcher or autostart start leaves nothing at all. The user clicks Ember and nothing happens; support has no log to read.
findings.evidence: Ran Electron as uid 65534 (setpriv) with EMBER_USER_DATA on a read-only directory: stderr 'Failed to create …/SingletonLock: Permission denied (13)', then {"msg":"instance.handover"}; the process ends with exit=0 and never opens a window. Same result when the data path is a file ('readlink … Not a directory'). The `try { mkdirSync…chmodSync } catch { /* reported when used */ }` at main.ts:101 never reports it.
findings.fix: In the `!requestSingleInstanceLock()` branch, first check that userData is writable (fs.accessSync(userData, W_OK) or create and remove a probe file). If it isn't, call startupFailed(new Error("Ember can't write to <dir>. Fix its owner or permissions…")) so the user gets a dialog and exit code 1. Only then treat the false result as a handover to another instance.

findings.title: A settings.json saved with a UTF-8 BOM or as UTF-16 (PowerShell 5.1, older editors, deployment scripts) resets every setting, including consent and onboarding
findings.scenario: An admin or user pre-seeds or edits settings.json with `Set-Content -Encoding UTF8` or `Out-File` (Windows PowerShell 5.1 writes a BOM or UTF-16LE). readFileSync(file,'utf8') keeps the BOM, JSON.parse and lenientJson both fail, and read() falls into the 'cannot be read at all' branch: only the never-look list is salvaged. Character, size, grants, models and consent (so the user must onboard again) go back to defaults. Ember then rewrites the file and keeps the original as settings.json.bad-<time>.
findings.evidence: Harness h/settings-harness.ts over SettingsStore.load(): the same content loads fully when plain (character=wisp size=80 grants={gedit:act}); with a leading U+FEFF, or UTF-16LE with a BOM, the result is character=cinder size=60 grants={} with recoveredFrom=settings.json.bad-… and the notice 'Some of settings.json couldn't be used, so those settings went back to their defaults'. admin.ts:121 parseAdminPolicy has the same JSON.parse(raw) and would lock Ember down on a BOM.
findings.fix: Read the file as a Buffer: strip EF BB BF, decode UTF-16 LE/BE when the BOM says so, then parse. Do the same in parseAdminPolicy and in main.ts settingsText() (the doctor's WSL switch).

findings.title: A transient read error at start-up (antivirus or sync lock, NFS hiccup) makes Ember start on defaults without a notice, and the first change overwrites the user's real settings with no backup
findings.scenario: settings.json exists but readFileSync fails once with EBUSY, EPERM, EACCES or EIO while Ember starts (login-time scans). read(false) takes `this.current = DEFAULT_SETTINGS; return` (lines 306-313) for any error, not only ENOENT. Ember shows first-run onboarding again with no problem notice and no backup. The first save (a slider, any toggle) replaces the user's file with defaults plus that one change. Consent, SSH hosts, command consents and the never-look list are lost. The running case (running=true) already keeps the settings in use and raises a notice.
findings.evidence: Harness h/settings-harness.ts with fs.readFileSync made to throw EBUSY on its first call: load() returns character=cinder onboarded=false, lastProblem=null. After store.update({size:70}) the file contains defaults with size 70, and the folder holds only settings.json (no .bad-* copy).
findings.fix: At start-up retry a few times (50-200 ms) for EBUSY/EPERM/EACCES/EIO/ETIMEDOUT. If it still fails, run on defaults but call problem() and refuse to overwrite: copy the file to .bad-<ts> first, or keep saves in memory until it reads again, as the running case does.

findings.title: The settings window swallows failed saves: with a full or unwritable disk the first-run 'Start Ember' button, toggles and the size slider do nothing and show no error
findings.area: settings UX on failure / low disk
findings.scenario: SettingsStore.save() throws (ENOSPC, EDQUOT, EROFS, EACCES, a locked file after retries) and the IPC handler (main.ts:385-391) rejects. Every caller in the renderer does `void window.ember.updateSettings(...)` (lines 68, 137, 143, 148, 153, 495, 709, 720, 755, 816, 820, 826). On first run the user ticks 'I agree' and presses 'Start Ember', and nothing happens and nothing explains why. Toggles keep their new look although nothing was saved or applied.
findings.evidence: Playwright against the real app with settings.json replaced by a directory (all saves fail with EISDIR): after clicking 'I agree' + 'Start Ember' the page's only trace is a console pageerror "Error invoking remote method 'ember:update-settings': Error: EISDIR … rename … settings.json"; document.body.className is still 'first-run', #start-row is not hidden, and the screenshot (savefail-2.png in the scratch folder) shows an unchanged page with no message.
findings.fix: Route all saves through one helper that catches the rejection, shows a visible message ('Ember couldn't save your settings: <reason>') and restores the control's previous state. Let the main process also push the failure through IPC.settingsNotice. Do not leave the first-run Start button silent.

findings.title: Ember deletes the user's own ~/.config/autostart/ember.desktop at every launch while 'Start Ember when I log in' is off, and any other Ember with a different data folder rewrites it
findings.platforms: linux (windows and macOS login items follow the same sync-to-setting pattern)
findings.scenario: A user or admin enables autostart the usual Linux way (copying /usr/share/applications/ember.desktop into ~/.config/autostart, or GNOME Tweaks / Startup Applications, which write ember.desktop). Ember's own setting startAtLogin defaults to false, and main.ts:1084 calls sys.autostart.sync(false) at every start, so syncAutostart() sees a file that differs from `null` and rmSync()s it. Ember stops starting at login after the first run. A dev build, an AppImage, or any Ember started with another EMBER_USER_DATA shares the same autostart file and overwrites or deletes it too.
findings.evidence: Harness h/auto.ts: with a hand-made ember.desktop in place, syncAutostart(false, cmd, file) returns true and the file no longer exists. The settings window will then show the switch off.
findings.fix: Only remove or replace an entry Ember wrote (check for a marker such as X-Ember-Managed=true), or only touch the file when the setting actually changed during this run (on toggle, not on every start). Leave foreign entries alone and show their presence in the settings note.

findings.title: Audit retention is by whole months and enforced only at start-up, so entries outlive the administrator's auditRetentionDays by up to a month or more
findings.scenario: An organisation sets auditRetentionDays to 7 (or leaves the default 30) for privacy reasons. prune() only deletes a monthly file once the end of its month is older than the cutoff, and main.ts:1349 calls it once, at start. An entry from the 1st of a month stays about 38 days with retention 7, and about 61 days with the default 30. An Ember that runs for weeks (autostart, never quits) keeps older months until the next restart.
findings.evidence: Harness h/prune.ts with retention 7 days and an entry written on 1 Sep: still on disk on 15 Sep, 30 Sep and 2 Oct (31 days old), deleted only on 20 Oct (49 days).
findings.fix: Rewrite or trim files by line timestamp (or write per-day files), run prune daily (setInterval with unref) as well as at start, and apply the cutoff to the entry's own timestamp.

findings.title: The consent text says what you ask is kept only while Ember runs, but the audit log stores the task goal and result summary for 30+ days
findings.scenario: The first-run card says: 'a record of every action it took (kept 30 days) … What you ask and what Ember answers is kept only while it runs.' TaskManager writes goal (first 300 characters of the request) and summary (first 300 characters of the result) plus the window title to ~/.config/ember/audit/*.jsonl (tasks.ts:122 and :277). They stay on disk after Ember quits, longer than the label says (see the retention finding).
findings.evidence: audit-2026-10.jsonl from the real-app run contains {"event":"task","phase":"asked","goal":"Do the thing"} and {"phase":"done","summary":"All done."}. The journal copy already reduces these to sizes (audit.ts journalLine), so the authors treat them as sensitive.
findings.fix: Reword the card ('…a record of every action, including the task's goal and result, kept N days'), or store sizes only and keep goal and summary in memory like the conversation.

findings.title: If the system clock steps back (VM time sync after resume, NTP step), the character flies about 230,000 px off screen and takes ~0.6 s to return
findings.scenario: The overlay tick computes dt = (Date.now() - last)/1000. Follower.step clamps only the top (Math.min(dt, 0.05), follow.ts:85,87), so a negative dt passes through into the spring integration. After a resume or snapshot restore on a VM or VDI, or an NTP step back of seconds, Ember vanishes and flies back in.
findings.evidence: Harness h/follow.ts with the real Follower: after a cursor flick, one step with dt=-3 puts Ember at x=233157,y=186465 on a 1280x800 screen; it takes 39 frames (~624 ms) to settle, 24 of them more than 5000 px away.
findings.fix: Clamp dt to [0, 0.05] in Follower.step, and use a monotonic clock (performance.now()) for the tick.

findings.title: EMBER_LOG_LEVEL with an unrecognised value (uppercase, 'warning', 'trace') turns on debug logging instead of being ignored
findings.scenario: main.ts:105 casts process.env.EMBER_LOG_LEVEL to LogLevel without checking. For an unknown name ORDER[level] is undefined, `ORDER[lvl] < undefined` is false, and every line, debug included (sidecar and voice stderr, overlay detail), is written. Packaged builds honour the variable, so someone setting EMBER_LOG_LEVEL=WARN to quieten the log gets the noisiest one.
findings.evidence: Harness h/log.ts: level 'info' writes 2 of 3 test lines; 'INFO', 'warning', 'verbose' and 'trace' all write 3 of 3, including the debug line. (Rotation itself is fine: ember.log + .1-.3, about 20 MB at most.)
findings.fix: Lower-case the value and fall back to 'info' (with a warn line) when it is not one of debug, info, warn, error.

findings.title: No logging of GPU/utility process crashes, and no recovery or logging for crashes of the command, prompt, desk-view and ask windows' renderers
findings.scenario: Only the home, overlay, handle, ask and mic windows handle render-process-gone. Nothing listens to app 'child-process-gone', and the command window, prompt window (SSH password and consent cards, always on top) and desk view have no handler. A GPU-process crash loop, the usual cause of blank or black windows on VMs and RDP, leaves nothing in ember.log. A crashed prompt window stays on screen blank until the card times out.
findings.evidence: grep of app/ for child-process-gone, render-process-gone and revive( finds only revive.ts, voice.ts:260, ask.ts:120, overlay.ts:314, handle.ts:75 and main.ts:300. commands/window.ts and remote/prompt-window.ts handle only 'closed'. (Not exercised by forcing a crash.)
findings.fix: Add app.on('child-process-gone') and a web-contents-created hook that logs render-process-gone with the reason for every window, and apply revive() (or close-and-answer-no) to the command and prompt windows.

findings.title: Hand edits of settings.json leave an unbounded pile of settings.json.bad-<time> files, and a valid-JSON-but-out-of-range value is rewritten under the editor while the user is still typing
findings.scenario: With an editor that autosaves (VS Code, JetBrains), each intermediate invalid state while the user types creates a new .bad-<Date.now()> copy (keep() runs once per mtime and nothing prunes them). If the intermediate text parses but a value is out of range (size 800 on the way to 80), read(true) repairs and saves over the file immediately (lines 345-347), so the editor reports the file changed on disk.
findings.evidence: Harness h/edit.ts simulating four autosaves: three .bad-* backups, and the file rewritten by Ember at the 'size: 800' state.
findings.fix: Keep at most the last few backups (delete older .bad-* when making a new one). In running mode, for a repairable file wait for the file to be unchanged for a couple of seconds before rewriting it.

findings.title: A failing audit write turns a performed action into an error (possible retry), and a vanished audit folder disables Ember until restart
findings.scenario: AuditLog.write uses fs.appendFileSync with no handling. With a full disk or an exhausted quota (NFS home on RHEL) or a removed audit folder (cleanup tools), the decision entry throws before the step, which is safe, but the 'action' entry after a click, type or key throws inside Worker.act's try, the catch writes again and throws again, and the tool returns an error although the click was performed (a 'Send' may then be retried by the model). The constructor creates the directory only once, so every later write fails until Ember restarts.
findings.evidence: Code reading: audit.ts:35-40; worker.ts:1899-1925 (action audit inside try, audit again in catch), Worker.audit has no try/catch (worker.ts:3294-3297). Not run end to end.
findings.fix: Catch write errors in AuditLog.write (re-create the folder, fall back to the journal, raise a visible 'audit unavailable' status), and fail new steps closed with a clear message rather than reporting finished steps as failed.
